root_cause.text: `acpi_ec_setup()` failed to clean up ACPI EC handlers after `ec_install_handlers()` returned an error, so on reduced-hardware platforms a deferred probe left the address-space handler registered with a `struct acpi_ec *` context that was later freed by `acpi_ec_add()`, creating a dangling pointer use-after-free in `acpi_ec_space_handler()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `ec_install_handlers()` on `-EPROBE_DEFER` “has already started the EC and installed the address space handler with the struct acpi_ec pointer as handler context,” but `acpi_ec_setup()` “propagates the error without any cleanup,” and then `acpi_ec_add()` frees the object, leaving “a dangling handler context in ACPICA”; the patch fixes this by adding `ec_remove_handlers(ec);` in the `acpi_ec_setup()` error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure partially installed ACPI EC handlers are removed when setup fails.
intent_record.what: In the error path after `ec_install_handlers(ec, device, call_reg)` fails, a new call to `ec_remove_handlers(ec);` was inserted before the existing `if (ec == first_ec) first_ec = NULL;` cleanup.
intent_record.how: If handler installation fails, the code now explicitly removes any EC handlers that may have been partially installed before continuing error cleanup. This prevents leftover handlers from remaining registered after setup failure.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure partially installed ACPI EC handlers are removed when setup fails.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes failure cleanup in acpi_ec_setup() by removing partially installed ACPI EC handlers, preventing the dangling handler context and resulting use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This call installs the ACPI EC handlers, and the bug occurs when a failure from this path is not followed by cleanup, leaving a handler registered with a freed EC context.
This is the failure path that should have triggered teardown of partially installed handlers; the missing cleanup on this error path is the root cause of the dangling pointer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call installs the ACPI EC handlers; when it fails, the setup path did not properly clean up the partially installed handlers, allowing a registered handler to retain a pointer to a later-freed struct acpi_ec.

This is the error branch where cleanup should have been performed after ec_install_handlers() failed; the missing teardown on this path is what left the dangling handler/context relationship in place.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function bodies already contain the handling added by this commit to avoid the problematic scope mismatch and cleanup issue. In `ec_install_handlers()`, the handler is installed at `scope_handle = ec == first_ec ? ACPI_ROOT_OBJECT : ec->handle`, and `acpi_execute_reg_methods()` also uses `scope_handle`, so the code is no longer limited to the EC device scope. In `ec_remove_handlers()`, removal also uses the same `scope_handle`, instead of the old `ec->address_space_handler_holder` path. In `acpi_ec_setup()`, the code now does `if (ret) { if (ec == first_ec) first_ec = NULL; return ret; }`, which explicitly cleans up the `first_ec` state on failure. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause—failing to clean up after `ec_install_handlers()` error leading to a dangling handler context—is not present in this snippet as shown.
